I've made the board's changes in `src/planning.rs` and a new `src/animations/steady.rs`, but **I couldn't compile or test them**. The build stops before type-checking for two reasons that aren't in this code. It can't read `.suspense/system-prompts/suspense-fluency.md`: the sandbox denies access to that folder, and I didn't try to get around that. And a stale build-script output points at template files under `/tmp` that no longer exist. The new code needs a build and a check in the running app before it can be relied on.

- **Panel opening:** when a story opens, its card's position is checked against the view as it will be once the board has narrowed. The board then scrolls sideways in the panel's own 150 ms motion. If the card was fully in view before, it stays fully in view; a card that was already partly hidden is left alone. Opening from the keyboard works this way.
- **Opened from outside the board, or by clicking:** a proposal's "Added to …" link, opening a story from elsewhere in the app, and clicking a card all scroll the board sideways and the card's column up or down until the card is fully in view. Each scroll stops with the card at the nearest edge. A card already fully in view scrolls nothing. If the card hasn't been drawn yet, as with a story just accepted, the scroll waits a frame for it.
- **Changes above the view:** in a column scrolled away from its top, the first card in view is tracked from frame to frame. When cards above the view are added, deleted or change height, the column's scroll shifts by the same amount at once, before anything is drawn, so the cards in view stay put. The card-slide animation is told about the shift, so those cards don't slide either. A column at its top keeps its top.

I found no palette or ribbon action that opens a story today. If one is added, it should open the story the same way the "Added to …" link does so it gets the same scrolling.
